As of March 31, 2026, LaSalle managed approximately $86.8 billion of public and private real estate assets and had over 825 employees in 22 offices in 13 countries. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Investment Objectives</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our investment objectives are to invest primarily in RE Debt Investments secured by high quality assets that will enable us to&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">provide current income in the form of regular, stable cash distributions to shareholders to achieve an attractive distribution yield&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">preserve and protect invested capital by focusing on high quality real assets with current cash flow and&#47;or limited business plan risks&#59; In some cases, we may originate and fund a first mortgage loan with the intention of selling the senior tranche (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">A Note</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) and retaining the subordinated tranche (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">B Note</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) or mezzanine loan tranche. We may receive loan origination fees, extension fees, exit fees, prepayment fees, loan assumption fees and other similar fees paid by borrowers in connection with the origination of each new loan (collectively, &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loan Fees</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), 50% of which will be paid to LaSalle, or an affiliate thereof, and 50% of which will be retained by us, and for our benefit. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Subordinate Debt</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58; We may originate or acquire mezzanine loans, which are loans made to property owners that are secured by pledges of the borrower&#8217;s ownership interests in the property and&#47;or the property owner. Mezzanine loans are subordinate to mortgage loans secured by mortgage liens on the property but are senior to the borrower&#8217;s equity in the property. Upon default, the mezzanine lender can foreclose on the ownership interests pledged under the loan and thereby succeed to ownership of the property, subject to the mortgage lien on the property. We may receive Loan Fees in connection with our mezzanine loans. We may originate or acquire &#8220;B Notes&#8221; in negotiated transactions with the originators and in the secondary market. A &#8220;B Note&#8221; is typically a privately negotiated loan that is secured by a first mortgage on a single large commercial property or group of related properties and subordinated to an &#8220;A Note&#8221; secured by the same first mortgage on the same property or group. The subordination of a &#8220;B Note&#8221; typically is evidenced by a co-lender agreement with the holder of the related &#8220;A Note.&#8221; &#8220;B Notes&#8221; are subject to more credit risk with respect to the underlying mortgage collateral than the corresponding &#8220;A Note.&#8221; We may receive Loan Fees in connection with our &#8220;B Note&#8221; investments. We may also seek to structure subordinate debt in the form of preferred equity investments.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Other Real Estate-Related Debt and Equity Securities</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">To a lesser extent, we may invest in other real estate lending strategies and other real estate-related debt and equity investments, including (but not limited to) CMBS and commercial real estate CLOs. CMBS are securities that are collateralized by, or evidence ownership interests in, a mortgage loan secured by a single commercial property, or a partial or entire pool of mortgage loans secured by commercial properties. CLOs are securities that are collateralized by a pool of debt obligations. We may invest in investment grade CMBS and&#47;or CLOs (rated BBB- or Baa3 or higher), sub-investment grade CMBS and&#47;or CLOs and&#47;or unrated CMBS and&#47;or CLOs. In general, we intend to invest in investment grade CMBS and&#47;or CLOs that will yield attractive current interest income. The yields on CMBS and&#47;or CLOs depend on the timely payment of interest on and principal of the underlying mortgage loans, and defaults by the borrowers under such loans may ultimately result in deficiencies and defaults on the CMBS and&#47;or CLOs. We believe our real estate-related debt and equity securities will help maintain liquidity to satisfy any share redemptions we choose to make in any particular quarter and manage cash before investing subscription proceeds into targeted investments while also seeking attractive current income. In addition, we may invest in CMBS and CLOs on a tactical basis to endeavor to take advantage of market opportunities. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">8</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Cash, Cash Equivalents and Other Short-Term Investments</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to hold cash, cash equivalents and other short-term investments. We will primarily target real estate with a &#8220;core plus&#8221; (moderate risk) profile, but we may also originate or acquire real estate loans with &#8220;core&#8221; (lower risk) and &#8220;high yield&#8221; (higher risk) profiles.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Core</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58; Lower-risk investment style secured by properties with stable cash flows without significant near-term lease expirations or material renovations needed.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Core-Plus</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58;  Moderate risk profile such as (1) loans secured by transitioning properties requiring leasing and&#47;or moderate renovations and (2) modest leverage on senior loans (typically 60% to 75% loan-to-value ratio (&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">LTV</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;)).</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">High Yield</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58; Higher risk and return metrics for investments such as&#58; (1) transitional loans secured by properties requiring significant development or repositioning, (2) mezzanine debt and preferred equity (typically 75% to 85% LTV), (3) construction loans at varying leverage levels, (4) riskier borrower profiles and (5) distressed debt.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Market Opportunity</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Commercial real estate is a capital-intensive business that relies heavily on debt capital to develop, acquire, maintain and refinance commercial properties. Ongoing availability of mortgage debt financing is basic to the success of commercial real estate owners and the commercial real estate industry at large. We believe that the current commercial real estate debt market presents a compelling opportunity for our investment strategy to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe RE debt investments present attractive investment opportunities for the following reasons&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Attractive risk-adjusted returns&#58; Real estate debt can offer compelling returns relative to other fixed income alternatives. The potential for achieving these higher yields, while maintaining a relatively conservative risk profile, is appealing to investors looking to mitigate risk. Real estate debt can offer different opportunities through the market cycle, with the ability to adjust advance rates during market downturns to minimize risk, while benefiting from cyclical recoveries.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Stable and predictable income&#58; An allocation to real estate debt may allow investors to enhance their portfolio income returns. The coupon-like nature of interest payments from borrowers can provide consistent and stable cash flows for investors, with a significant portion of the total return being achieved through income returns.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Downside protection and capital preservation&#58; Real estate debt offers the ability for investors to gain exposure to the same underlying real estate, but via a protected position in the capital structure, offering an often-significant equity cushion to buffer against potential value fluctuations.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Diversification benefits&#58; Real estate debt provides exposure to one of the largest segments of the real estate market, typically with lower volatility than real estate equity. And adding real estate debt to a portfolio can enhance diversification, as it often has low correlation with traditional asset classes like stocks and bonds, which can help to improve overall risk-adjusted returns.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Inflation hedge&#58; As inflation rises, so too do the interest rates central banks often use to combat it. Real estate debt investments, particularly those with floating-rate loans linked to central bank rates, can therefore offer some protection against inflation.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">10</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe LaSalle&#8217;s experience managing real estate debt funds for over 20 years will allow us to capitalize on these opportunities through their expertise and capabilities valuing real estate collateral and evaluating market trends to help us identify value and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Potential Competitive Strengths</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We believe our most powerful potential competitive strength is our affiliation with LaSalle, whose global real estate debt and equity investing platform has market leverage embedded within it since its inception over 45 years ago. LaSalle, our investment advisor, and JLL, our Sponsor, bring over 200 years of real estate experience to help identify what we believe to be the best performing geographic market and property sector combinations to achieve our targeted risk&#47;return objectives. JLL is powered by rich global datasets and leading technology capabilities, which allows it to provide effective, coordinated services and successfully navigate the dynamic and challenging markets in which it competes worldwide.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">JLL is distinguished in the market for its commitment to investing in technology and data capabilities, including AI, data, and technology, that drive productivity and client results. It is one of the most experienced real estate-focused investment managers in the industry, having launched its first institutional investment fund in 1979. LaSalle is an industry leader in property and facility management services and is one of the world&#8217;s premier diversified real estate investment management firms, with approximately $86.8 billion of assets under management as of March 31, 2026. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">11</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">LaSalle&#8217;s dedicated Americas debt investment team has more than 20 years of experience in first mortgage debt lending. The team&#8217;s first U.S. first mortgage, closed-end debt fund began investing in 2005 and experienced the global financial crisis (&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">GFC</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;). Across these funds the investment team has originated over 500 loans totaling approximately $6.6 billion in gross volume. Importantly, there is significant tenure across all senior members of the team. We believe our underwriting benefits from LaSalle&#8217;s position as both a lender and, through its broader real estate platform, an equity owner and operator of real estate. This dual perspective gives our underwriting team access to current, firm-wide data on occupancy trends, operating expenses, sales prices, renewal rates and renovation costs and timelines, informing our view on new originations to a degree we believe exceeds managers without comparable in-house operating experience.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline"> </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">JLL and LaSalle together provide the Company with a distinct combination of global commercial real estate services and institutional investment management expertise. This alignment of strengths is one that we believe will only grow more valuable as markets evolve and competition for attractive opportunities increases. We believe this affiliation positions our company to identify and capitalize on attractive opportunities, prudently manage risk, and deliver long-term value to our investors.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">LaSalle&#8217;s Investment Approach and Identification of Investments</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">LaSalle&#8217;s investment process includes sourcing, underwriting, structuring, approving, closing, servicing, and, if applicable, exiting each investment. LaSalle utilizes a broad real estate research and platform strategy to identify investment opportunities, drawing on the extensive local presence of JLL professionals throughout the world to gather and share proprietary insight into local market conditions. In addition, LaSalle&#8217;s in-house Research and Strategy team is actively involved in setting strategy and making investment decisions, employing a data-driven approach to identify prime sectors and geographic markets for investment. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">LaSalle&#8217;s U.S. debt team has completed over $6 billion in first mortgage transactions over the past 20 years, investing across a broad range of asset classes in 37 U.S. states. The team targets tactical opportunities in select markets, prioritizing attributes such as barriers to new development, sustained job growth and regions with diverse economies. The integrated nature of LaSalle&#8217;s origination and underwriting team is designed to provide end-to-end confidence in the assets, markets, sponsors and business plans that loans fund. Over 80% of LaSalle&#8217;s business is via repeat broker or borrower relationships, reflecting the team&#8217;s relationship-driven origination model and reputation for quick and efficient closing. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Each potential investment undergoes a multi-layered investment process. Due diligence is led by the originations and underwriting team responsible for sourcing the investment opportunity, working in conjunction with LaSalle&#8217;s US Debt portfolio management team, asset management team and legal counsel. Thorough underwriting and diligence is conducted on each investment including an evaluation of historic property performance and financials, an in-person property inspection, a sponsor analysis, a business plan analysis, third-party report reviews and a detailed financial underwriting of the asset over the loan term. The originations and underwriting team receive and review a substantial amount of diligence items from the borrower including income statements, balance sheets, rent rolls, leases, utility bills, tax bills, insurance policies, bank statements, occupancy trend reports, renovation budgets, service contracts, title reports, form leases, management agreements, operating agreements and organizational documents. In addition to materials received from the borrower, third-party reports received include appraisals, environmental reports, property condition reports, zoning reports, insurance reports, real estate tax reviews, budget cost reviews, seismic reports, crime reports, credit checks and legal searches. Each transaction is underwritten with a bottom-up method through an equity owner&#8217;s lens and a top-down method through a macro-research lens to help ensure that all interests are aligned and that there is a clear exit strategy. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">12</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">LaSalle&#8217;s research-driven approach to market and asset selection is central to our investment process. Investment decisions are informed by a three-part internal research process&#58; (i) macro-level strategic research forecasting return and risk prospects across regions and property types, taking into account growth prospects, liquidity, supply constraints and barriers to entry&#59; (ii) a proprietary market ranking methodology that evaluates target markets for debt investment using both traditional real estate metrics and debt-specific considerations such as foreclosure practicability and volatility&#59; and (iii) an independent, asset-specific market report prepared for each potential investment, examining the local economy, competitive supply and submarket fundamentals. This research capability is supported by LaSalle&#8217;s global research team, complemented by access to JLL&#8217;s broader global research network. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">All investment decisions are subject to the approval of LaSalle&#8217;s US Debt Investment Committee, which is comprised of six senior members of the LaSalle Americas management and debt teams, prior to execution. The Company will receive approval from the US Debt Investment Committee for its annual strategic plans.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Borrowing Policies</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to use leverage to provide additional funds to support our investment activities and aim to enhance our return. After we have raised substantial proceeds in our offering and aggregated a diversified portfolio of investments (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Ramp-Up Period</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), our target leverage ratio is expected to be 60% to 80% on a portfolio-wide basis. Our leverage ratio will be measured by dividing (i) the aggregate principal amount of our outstanding indebtedness (including both entity-level and investment-level debt), by (ii) the gross asset value of our investments (measured using the greater of fair market value and cost). For purposes of calculating our leverage, we exclude (1) any senior portions of investments that are sold to, or held by, third party lenders to achieve &#8220;structural leverage,&#8221; where we retain a second lien, mezzanine or other subordinate investment that is unencumbered and not otherwise pledged as collateral for borrowed money, (2) short-term indebtedness of us or our subsidiaries (that generally has a maturity of or that is intended to be repaid within 180 days or less), (3) any subscription or other financing facilities that are secured by commitments by investors to purchase our common shares and (4) intercompany loans or other indebtedness, including notes and rated notes issued to investors.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">During the Ramp-Up Period and at times of increased or decreased investment and capital market activity, we may employ greater leverage to build a broader and more diversified portfolio of investments. We may leverage our portfolio by assuming or incurring secured or unsecured investment-level and&#47;or entity-level debt. We may procure financing from LaSalle, JLL or their respective affiliates&#59; provided, that any such financing will be approved by a majority of the Board, including a majority of our independent trustees (each, an &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">independent trustee</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), not otherwise interested in the transaction as fair and competitive. We may decide to reserve borrowing capacity under any future lines of credit to be used to fund redemptions of our common shares in the event that redemption requests exceed our operating cash flows and net proceeds from our continuous private offering, to fund debt investments or for any other corporate purpose. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our actual leverage level will be affected by a number of factors, some of which are outside of our control (e.g., equity inflows and outflows, NAV changes, draws on lines of credit and subscription lines). Significant inflows of proceeds from the sale of our common shares generally will cause our leverage as a percentage of our net assets to decrease, at least temporarily. Significant outflows of equity as a result of redemptions of our common shares generally will cause our leverage as a percentage of our net assets to increase, at least temporarily. Our leverage as a percentage of our net assets will also increase or decrease with decreases or increases, respectively, in the NAV of our portfolio. If we borrow under a line of credit to fund redemptions of our common shares or for other purposes, our leverage would increase and may exceed our target leverage. In such cases, our leverage may remain at the higher level until we receive additional net proceeds from our continuous private offering or sell some of our assets to repay outstanding indebtedness.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">13</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">There is, however, no limit on the amount we may borrow with respect to any individual investment or on a portfolio-wide basis. During the Ramp-Up Period, our leverage ratio may exceed our target. We may also exceed our target leverage ratio at times, particularly during a market downturn or in connection with a large acquisition. Our board of trustees will periodically review our aggregate borrowings. In connection with such review, our board of trustees may determine to modify our target leverage ratio in light of then-current economic conditions, relative costs of debt and equity capital, fair values of our investments, general conditions in the market for debt investments, growth and investment opportunities or other factors.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Financing Arrangements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In addition to entity-level borrowing facilities we may enter into, we expect to incur indebtedness through other financing arrangements described below. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Direct Leverage</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We may elect to borrow against our debt investments through the following kinds of arrangements&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Loan Facilities</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Warehouse Facility</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58;  We may use warehouse credit facilities, such as repurchase agreements, to finance debt investments.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Asset Specific Financing</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58;  We may use asset specific financing to finance a pre-identified credit investment. Defining characteristics of such financings generally include&#58; matched term, no margin call rights, partial to no recourse and no cross collateralization with other credit assets.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Term Loan Financing</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58; We may use term loan financing to finance a pre-identified pool of debt investments.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Securitization</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We may choose to contribute all or a subset of the RE Debt Investments in the portfolio to an asset-backed securitized offering, such as a commercial real estate collateralized loan obligation, CMBS or some other structured finance vehicle. Defining characteristics generally include&#58; matched term, no margin call rights, no recourse, and cross collateralization with other credit assets on the same securitization.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Structural Leverage</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We may elect to reduce our position in the whole loans through co-origination or &#8220;A&#160;Note&#8221; sales, which will eliminate our exposure or liability associated with the senior tranche of the loan, as described below&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Co-Origination</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58;  We may co-originate a whole loan in conjunction with a senior lender and simultaneously close on the junior tranche. This structure allows for matched-term and generally non-recourse financing of the portfolio, without cross-collateralization.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">&#8220;A&#160;Note&#8221; Sales</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#58;  We may split a whole loan into two pieces (senior tranche &#47; junior tranche) and sell the senior tranche to a third-party. This structure allows for matched-term and generally non-recourse financing, without cross-collateralization.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">14</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Temporary Strategies</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">During the Ramp-Up Period and&#47;or during periods in which LaSalle determines that economic or market conditions are unfavorable to investors and a defensive strategy would benefit us, we may temporarily depart from our investment strategy. During these periods, subject to compliance with the Investment Company Act, we may expand or change our investment strategy and target assets, including by investing all or any portion of our assets in U.S. government securities, including bills, notes and bonds differing as to maturity and rates of interest that are either issued or guaranteed by the U.S. Treasury or by U.S. government agencies or instrumentalities&#59; non-U.S. government securities that have received the highest investment grade credit rating&#59; certificates of deposit issued against funds deposited in a bank or a savings and loan association&#59; commercial paper&#59; bankers&#8217; acceptances&#59; fixed time deposits&#59; shares of money market funds&#59; credit-linked notes&#59; repurchase agreements with respect to any of the foregoing&#59; or any other fixed income securities that LaSalle considers consistent with this temporary strategy. During these periods, we may also determine to pay down certain of our borrowings and have indebtedness below our target leverage ratio or we may borrow more to provide for additional liquidity causing us to exceed our target leverage ratio. It is impossible to predict when, or for how long, LaSalle will use these alternative strategies. Such strategies may not be successful. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Operating and Regulatory Structure</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">REIT Qualification</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to elect and qualify to be taxed as a REIT under the Code commencing with our taxable year ending December 31, 2026. We believe that we are organized and will operate in such a manner as to qualify for taxation as a REIT under the applicable provisions of the Code so long as our board of trustees determines that REIT qualification remains in our best interest. So long as we qualify as a REIT, we generally will not be subject to U.S. federal income tax on REIT taxable income that we distribute annually to our shareholders. In order to qualify as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we must continually satisfy tests concerning, among other things, the real estate qualification of sources of our income, the composition and values of our assets, the amounts we distribute to our shareholders and the diversity of ownership of our common shares. In order to comply with REIT requirements, we may need to forgo otherwise attractive opportunities and limit our expansion opportunities and limit the manner in which we conduct our operations. See &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Risk Factors&#8212;Risks Related to our REIT Status and Certain Other Tax Items</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.&#8221;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Investment Company Act Considerations</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are not registered, and do not intend to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act. Under the Investment Company Act, in relevant part, a company is an &#8220;investment company&#8221; if&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">under Section 3(a)(1)(A), it is, or holds itself out as being, engaged primarily, or proposes to engage primarily, in the business of investing, reinvesting or trading in securities&#59; or</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">under Section 3(a)(1)(C), it is engaged, or proposes to engage in, the business of investing, reinvesting, owning, holding or trading in securities and owns, or proposes to acquire, &#8220;investment securities&#8221; having a value exceeding 40% of the value of its total assets (exclusive of U.S. government securities and cash items) on an unconsolidated basis. The term &#8220;investment securities&#8221; generally includes all securities except U.S. government securities and securities of majority-owned subsidiaries that are not themselves investment companies and are not relying on the exemption from the definition of investment company under Section 3(c)(1) or Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">15</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">With respect to Section 3(a)(1)(A), we do not intend to engage primarily or hold ourselves out as being engaged primarily in the business of investing, reinvesting or trading in securities. Rather, we will be a holding company primarily engaged in the non-investment company businesses of our subsidiaries. With respect to Section 3(a)(1)(C), on an unconsolidated basis we expect that more than 60% of our assets, exclusive of cash and U.S. government securities, will consist of ownership interests in wholly-owned subsidiaries that are not themselves investment companies and are not relying on the exceptions from the definition of investment company under Section 3(c)(1) or Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act and, thus, we do not expect that more than 40% of our assets, exclusive of cash and U.S. government securities, will be &#8220;investment securities,&#8221; as that term is used under the Investment Company Act.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">If, however, we are deemed for any reason to fall within the definition of an &#8220;investment company&#8221; under Section 3(a)(1) of the Investment Company Act, we believe we will be able to rely on the exemption provided by Section 3(c)(6) of the Investment Company Act, which excludes from the definition of &#8220;investment company&#8221; any company primarily engaged, directly or through majority-owned subsidiaries, in one or more of the businesses described in paragraphs (3), (4), and (5) of Section 3(c), or in one or more such businesses (from which not less than 25% of such company&#8217;s gross income during its last fiscal year was derived) together with an additional business or businesses other than investing, reinvesting, owning, holding, or trading in securities. We expect to be &#8220;primarily engaged,&#8221; directly or through majority-owned subsidiaries, in the businesses described in Section 3(c)(5) because our majority-owned subsidiaries intend to rely on Section 3(c)(5)(C) (described below) as entities primarily engaged in acquiring mortgages and other liens on and interests in real estate. As a result, we expect our assets to be deployed, and our income to be derived, predominantly from Section 3(c)(5)(C) businesses. Accordingly, the Company believes it could continue to rely on Section 3(c)(6) so long as our majority-owned subsidiaries qualify for the Section 3(c)(5)(C) exemption and we remain primarily engaged in those businesses (including, where applicable, deriving not less than 25% of our gross income from such businesses together with any additional non-securities business permitted by Section 3(c)(6)).</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Section 3(c)(5)(C) of the Investment Company Act provides an exemption from the definition of an &#8220;investment company&#8221;. Section 3(c)(5)(C) is available for entities &#8220;primarily engaged in the business of purchasing or otherwise acquiring mortgages and other liens on and interests in real estate.&#8221; This exemption generally requires that, for purposes of Section 3(c)(5)(C), at least 55% of an entity&#8217;s portfolio must be composed of &#8220;Qualifying Interests&#8221; and at least 80% of its portfolio must be composed of Qualifying Interests and &#8220;Real Estate-Related Interests&#8221; (and no more than 20% composed of non-qualifying or non-real estate-related assets). These criteria therefore limit the types of assets that these subsidiaries may acquire and dispose of.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Qualifying Interests for purposes of Section 3(c)(5)(C) include mortgage loans and other assets, such as certain mezzanine loans, residual interests, and other interests in real estate as interpreted by the SEC staff in various no-action letters. We also may invest in transitional loans or mortgage loan participations that also meet the parameters of Section 3(c)(5)(C) based on no-action letters issued by the SEC staff and other SEC interpretive guidance. Based on this guidance, assets that may constitute Real Estate-Related Interests (but not Qualifying Interests) include mortgage-backed securities that represent less than the entire ownership in a pool of mortgage loans, debt and equity tranches of securitizations, certain real estate-related asset-backed securities and debt or equity securities issued by companies primarily engaged in the business of purchasing mortgages or other interests in real estate. Assets that are not expected to constitute either Qualifying Interests or Real Estate-Related Interests include non-real estate-related asset-backed securities, corporate debt or equity securities of companies not primarily engaged in real estate, and other assets that do not have a sufficient nexus to real estate.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to treat first mortgage loans as Qualifying Interests, as long as such loans are &#8220;fully secured&#8221; by real estate at the time we acquire the loan. Mortgage loans that are junior to a mortgage held by another lender, or second mortgages, will also be treated as Qualifying Interests if the real property fully secures such junior mortgage.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">16</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to treat subordinated participation interests as Qualifying Interests only if&#58; (1) we have a participation interest in a mortgage loan that is fully secured by real property&#59; (2) we have the right to receive our proportionate share of the interest and the principal payments made on the loan by the borrower, and our returns on the loan are based on such payments&#59; (3) we invest only after performing the same type of due diligence and credit underwriting procedures that we would perform if we were underwriting the underlying mortgage loan&#59; (4) we have approval rights in connection with any material decisions pertaining to the administration and servicing of the loan and with respect to any material modification to the loan agreements&#59; and (5) in the event that the loan becomes non-performing, we have effective control over the remedies relating to the enforcement of the mortgage loan, including ultimate control of the foreclosure process, by having the right to&#58; (a) appoint the special servicer to manage the resolution of the loan&#59; (b) advise, direct or approve the actions of the special servicer&#59; (c) terminate the special servicer at any time with or without cause&#59; (d) cure the default so that the mortgage loan is no longer non-performing&#59; and (e) purchase the senior participation at par plus accrued interest, thereby acquiring the entire mortgage loan.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to treat most types of CMBS, non-qualifying subordinated financing, and any debt or equity securities issued by companies primarily engaged in the business of purchasing mortgages or other interests in real estate as Real Estate-Related Interests.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Although we intend to monitor our portfolio periodically and prior to each investment acquisition and disposition, there can be no guarantee that we will successfully maintain our assets at the necessary levels. To the extent that the SEC staff provides more specific guidance regarding any of the matters bearing upon such exemptions, we may be required to adjust our strategy accordingly. Any additional guidance from the SEC staff could provide additional flexibility to us, or it could further inhibit our ability to pursue the strategies we have chosen.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Operating Structure and REIT Considerations</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A non-listed REIT is a REIT whose common shares are not listed for trading on a stock exchange or other securities market. We use the term &#8220;perpetual-life REIT&#8221; to describe an investment vehicle of indefinite duration, whose common shares are intended to be sold by the Company on a continuous basis at a price generally equal to the Company&#8217;s prior month&#8217;s NAV per share.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We intend to elect and qualify to be taxed as a REIT under the Code commencing with our taxable year ending December 31, 2026, and we intend to continue to make such an election. In general, a REIT is a company that&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">combines the capital of many investors to acquire or provide financing for real estate assets&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">offers the benefits of a real estate portfolio under professional management&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">satisfies the various requirements of the Code, including a requirement to distribute to shareholders at least 90% of its REIT taxable income (determined without regard to the dividends-paid deduction and excluding net capital gain) each year&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">is generally not subject to U.S. federal corporate income taxes on its REIT taxable income that it currently distributes to its shareholders, which substantially eliminates the &#8220;double taxation&#8221; (i.e., taxation at both the corporate and shareholder levels) that generally results from investments in a C corporation.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In order to comply with REIT requirements, we may need to forgo otherwise attractive opportunities and limit our expansion opportunities and limit the manner in which we conduct our operations. See &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8212;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Risks Related to our REIT Status and Certain Other Tax Items</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.&#8221;</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">17</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The following chart shows our current ownership structure and our relationship with our Sponsor, LaSalle, and their respective affiliates, as of the date of this Registration Statement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><img alt="business1aa.jpg" src="business1aa.jpg" style="height:540px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:537px"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Board of Trustees</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We operate under the direction of our board of trustees. Our board of trustees will retain LaSalle to manage the origination, acquisition and dispositions of our investments, subject to our board of trustees&#8217; supervision.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">18</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Upon the initial closing (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Initial Private Wealth Closing</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) of our continuous, blind pool private offering that includes investors other than LaSalle, the Sponsor and&#47;or their respective affiliates, we will have a five-member board. A majority of our entire board of trustees may change the number of trustees from time to time, provided that the total number may not be less than one (1) and not more than fifteen (15), provided further that following the Initial Private Wealth Closing and unless we amend our Bylaws, the total number may not be less than three (3) and not more than fifteen (15). Our Bylaws provide that, following the Initial Private Wealth Closing, a majority of our trustees must be independent trustees, except for a period of up to 60 days after the death, removal or resignation of, or other vacancy involving, an independent trustee pending the election of a successor independent trustee. Our Declaration of Trust defines &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">independent trustee</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; as a trustee (a) who is not an officer or employee of the Company, any subsidiary of the Company, or LaSalle, the Sponsor or their respective affiliates, (b) whom the Board affirmatively determines has no material relationship with the Company and (c) who otherwise satisfies the trustee independence tests provided for in Section 303A.02 of the New York Stock Exchange Listed Company Manual, as may be amended from time to time. We expect our board of trustees will determine that three trustees are independent trustees, giving us a majority independent board of trustees in connection with the Initial Private Wealth Closing.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Following the Initial Private Wealth Closing, for so long as LaSalle or its affiliate acts as investment advisor to us, LaSalle has the right to designate two trustees to our board of trustees, provided the board of trustees remains majority independent. Our board of trustees must also consult with LaSalle in connection with filling any vacancies created by the removal, resignation, retirement or death of any trustee (other than in connection with a removal by shareholders in accordance with our Declaration of Trust) following the Initial Private Wealth Closing. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Each trustee will serve until his or her resignation, removal, death, or adjudication of legal incompetence or the election and qualification of his or her successor. Although the number of trustees may be increased or decreased, a decrease may not shorten the term of any incumbent trustee. Any trustee may resign at any time or may be removed by the shareholders only for &#8220;cause,&#8221; and then only upon the affirmative vote of shareholders entitled to cast at least two-thirds of all the votes entitled to be cast on the matter. In addition, any trustee may be removed, at any time, but only for &#8220;cause&#8221; by written instrument, signed by a majority of the trustees, specifying the date when such removal shall become effective. For so long as LaSalle has the right to designate trustees to our board of trustees, LaSalle may remove, with or without cause, any trustee designated by LaSalle, by delivering written notice to our board of trustees specifying the date when such removal shall become effective. A vacancy on our board of trustees resulting from any reason other than removal for &#8220;cause&#8221; by the shareholders, may be filled only by a vote of a majority of the remaining trustees&#59; provided that, following the Initial Private Wealth Closing, any vacancy involving an independent trustee may be filled only by a vote of a majority of the remaining independent trustees and any vacancy involving a trustee that was designated by LaSalle may be filled only by LaSalle. A vacancy on our board of trustees resulting from removal by the shareholders for &#8220;cause&#8221; or if there are no trustees may be filled only by the shareholders. &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Cause</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; is defined in our Declaration of Trust as conviction of a felony or a final judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction holding that such trustee caused demonstrable, material harm to the Company through bad faith or active and deliberate dishonesty.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our board of trustees will generally meet quarterly or more frequently if necessary. Our trustees are not required to devote all of their time to our business and are only required to devote the time to our business as their duties may require. In the event that the Company and LaSalle are unable to agree to the terms of the revised compensation to be payable to LaSalle during such 60-day period, the Advisory Agreement will terminate following the initial term or subsequent renewal term, as the case may be.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In addition, without penalty or fee, the Advisory Agreement may be terminated (i) at the option of LaSalle (A)&#160;immediately for &#8220;cause&#8221; or (B) upon the bankruptcy of LaSalle. &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Cause</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; is defined in the Advisory Agreement (a) with respect to the termination of the Advisory Agreement by the Company, as fraud, criminal conduct, willful misconduct or willful or gross negligent breach of fiduciary duty by LaSalle in connection with performing its duties thereunder or the breach of a material provision of the Advisory Agreement by LaSalle after notice of such breach and a reasonable time to cure (to the extent that such breach is curable) or (b) with respect to the termination of the Advisory Agreement by LaSalle, as material breach by the Company of the Advisory Agreement after notice of such breach and reasonable time to cure (to the extent that such breach is curable). </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In the event the Advisory Agreement is terminated, LaSalle will be entitled to receive its prorated management fee and Performance Fee through the date of termination. In addition, upon the termination or expiration of the Advisory Agreement, LaSalle will cooperate with us and take all reasonable steps requested to assist our board of trustees in making an orderly transition of the advisory function.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Management Fee, Performance Fee and Expense Reimbursements </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management Fee</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. As compensation for its services provided pursuant to the Advisory Agreement, we will pay LaSalle a management fee of 1.25% of NAV for the outstanding Class S shares, Class D shares, and Class I shares, per annum, payable monthly in arrears. For the avoidance of doubt, we will not pay LaSalle the management fee with respect to the Class E shares, and as a result, it is a class-specific expense. In calculating the management fee, we will use our NAV before giving effect to accruals for the management fee, Performance Fee, shareholder servicing fees or distributions payable on our common shares. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Pursuant to the Advisory Agreement, to the extent that the Operating Partnership issues units to parties other than the Company, the Operating Partnership will pay LaSalle a management fee equal to 1.25% of the NAV of the Operating Partnership attributable to such Class S, Class D and Class I Operating Partnership units not held by the Company, per annum payable monthly. </font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">22</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The management fee may be paid, at LaSalle&#8217;s election, in cash or Class E shares, or any combination thereof. To the extent that LaSalle elects to receive any portion of the management fee in Class E shares, we may redeem such Class E shares from LaSalle at a later date, at a price per Class E share equal to the NAV per Class E share, as of the date of redemption. Our Class E shares obtained by LaSalle will not be subject to our share redemption program, including the redemption limits and any Early Redemption Deduction (as defined below).</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Performance Fee</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. For Class S Shares, Class D Shares and Class I Shares (collectively, the &#8220;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance Shares</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), LaSalle may be entitled to a Performance Fee (the &#8220;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance Fee</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), which is accrued monthly and payable quarterly in arrears. The Performance Fee will be an amount, not less than zero, equal to (i) 12.5% of our cumulative Core Earnings (as defined below) for the immediately preceding four calendar quarters, or such shorter period until the Company has operated for four calendar quarters (each such period, a &#8220;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">4-Quarter&#160;Performance Measurement Period</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), subject to a hurdle rate, expressed as an annual rate of return on average adjusted capital, equal to 1.25% per calendar quarter, or 5.0% on an annualized basis (the &#8220;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Hurdle Rate</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), minus (ii)&#160;the sum of any Performance Fees paid to LaSalle with respect to the first three calendar quarters in the applicable&#160;4-Quarter&#160;Performance Measurement Period. As a result, LaSalle does not earn a Performance Fee for any calendar quarter until our Core Earnings for the applicable&#160;4-Quarter&#160;Performance Measurement Period exceed the Hurdle Rate. For purposes of the Performance Fee, &#8220;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">adjusted capital</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; means cumulative net proceeds generated from sales of our Performance Shares (including proceeds from our distribution reinvestment plan) reduced for distributions from&#160;non-liquidating&#160;dispositions of our investments paid to shareholders holding Performance Shares and amounts paid to shareholders holding Performance Shares for share redemptions pursuant to our share redemption program.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Once the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings in any calendar quarter exceed the Hurdle Rate, LaSalle is entitled to a &#8220;catch-up&#8221; fee equal to the amount of Core Earnings in excess of the Hurdle Rate, until the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period exceed a percentage of average adjusted capital equal to the Hurdle Rate divided by 0.875 (or 1 minus 0.125) for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period. Thereafter, LaSalle is entitled to receive 12.5% of the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings.  </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Performance Fees are accrued monthly and payable quarterly, in arrears. For the avoidance of doubt, we will not pay LaSalle a Performance Fee on Class E shares, and as a result, it is a class-specific expense. LaSalle believes there has been to date, and expects there to continue to be, sufficient investment opportunities for the Company within its investment guidelines because of the scale of the real estate debt markets. At times there may be overlap of the Company&#8217;s investment opportunities with certain Other LaSalle Accounts that are actively investing and may be similar overlap with future Other LaSalle Accounts. In some instances conflicts may occur when a particular investment meets the stated investment parameters of more than one Other LaSalle Account. LaSalle employs an established allocation policy to address potentially competing client demands. The allocation process is designed to be fair and equitable to all Other LaSalle Accounts to the fullest extent possible. In particular, no Other LaSalle Account shall receive preferential treatment in the process due to its status as an affiliate or non-affiliate of LaSalle. Other LaSalle Account eligibility for any specific allocation shall be determined by the Other LaSalle Account&#8217;s portfolio manager and by the investment allocator (a designated staff member of LaSalle&#8217;s portfolio management team), taking into consideration the Other LaSalle Account&#8217;s investment criteria, return requirements and remaining investment need. The portfolio manager will serve as the Company&#8217;s advocate in the allocation process, except that the allocator shall serve in a neutral role specifically regarding his or her duties as allocator. If multiple Other LaSalle Accounts are eligible for an investment, a rotational queue process is followed to determine the allocation of the investment. Currently, certain Other LaSalle Accounts that invest in RE Debt Investments with overlapping investment objectives have a priority to us over RE Debt Investments that meet certain size and other characteristics, and certain RE Debt Investments will be first offered to such Other LaSalle Accounts. Other LaSalle Accounts having priority over us will result in fewer investment opportunities being made available to us.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">While LaSalle will seek to manage potential conflicts of interest in a fair and reasonable manner as required by the Advisory Agreement, the portfolio strategies employed by LaSalle and its affiliates in managing the Other LaSalle Accounts could conflict with the strategies employed by LaSalle in managing our business and may adversely affect the marketability, exit strategy, prices and availability of the properties, securities and instruments in which we invest.
