&#8220;Company&#8221; refer to JLL Property Finance Trust.</font></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_468"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 1. Organization</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">JLL Property Finance Trust was formed on</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> August 11</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, 2026, as a Maryland statutory trust and expects to qualify as a real estate investment trust (&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">REIT</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) for federal income tax purposes. The Company&#8217;s sponsor is Jones Lang LaSalle Incorporated (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Sponsor</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;). LaSalle Investment Management, Inc. (&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">LaSalle</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Advisor</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) will serve as the external advisor to the Company.  The Company intends to conduct its operations and own all or substantially all of its assets through PFT Operating Partnership LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Operating Partnership</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) which is a consolidated subsidiary.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company will seek to (1) provide shareholders with current income in the form of regular, stable cash distributions to achieve an attractive distribution yield&#59; (2) preserve and protect shareholders&#8217; invested capital by focusing on high quality real estate assets that typically have current cash-flow and&#47;or limited business plan risk&#59; (3) reduce downside risk through conservative loan-to-value ratios against high quality real estate assets with meaningful borrower equity or implied equity&#59; and (4) provide an investment alternative for shareholders seeking to allocate a portion of their investment portfolios to real estate debt with lower volatility than publicly traded securities and compelling risk-adjusted returns compared to traditional fixed income alternatives.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company&#8217;s primary investment strategy is to originate, acquire, finance, manage and dispose of a portfolio consisting primarily of real estate debt investments, including senior mortgage loans, subordinated debt and other similar investments, diversified across both geography and underlying property sectors. The real estate loans are expected to be secured by properties located in the United States and include a broad range of investment property types primarily in, but not limited to, multifamily, industrial, hospitality, lifestyle and grocery anchored retail, flex and mixed-use, office, self-storage, industrial outdoor storage, single-family rentals, senior housing, manufactured housing, life sciences, health care, medical outpatient, and to a lesser extent ground leases, net leases, cold storage, data centers, and other specialty property types. To a lesser extent, the Company may invest in other real estate lending strategies and other real estate-related debt and equity investments, including commercial mortgage-backed securities and commercial real estate collateralized loan obligations and&#47;or cash equivalent investments. No investments have been purchased or contracted to be purchased as of the balance sheet date.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company will be a &#8220;perpetual-life REIT,&#8221; meaning the Company will be an investment vehicle of indefinite duration, whose shares are intended to be sold monthly on a continuous basis at a price generally equal to the Company&#8217;s prior month&#8217;s net asset value (&#8220;NAV&#8221;) per share.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On September</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> 9,</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> 2026 (date of initial capitalization), LaSalle invested $1,000 to capitalize the Company, for a consideration of </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">40 common shares of beneficial interest, par value $0.01 per share, of the Company. Because employees of the Sponsor have the ability to cause the Com</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">pany to repurchase the common shares issued for this investment for cash, the Company has classified these common shares as temporary (or &#8220;mezzanine&#8221;) equity on the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheet.</font></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_475"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 2. Significant Accounting Policies</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company believes the following significant accounting policies, among others, affect its significant estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of the consolidated financial statement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Basis of Accounting&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The accompanying consolidated financial statement has been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">GAAP</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;). Separate statements of operations, comprehensive income, shareholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows have not been presented because the Company has not commenced operations.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">F-4</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Use of Estimates&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The preparation of the consolidated financial statement in conformity with GAAP requires the Company to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of the balance sheet and the reported amounts of revenues. Actual results may ultimately differ materially from those estimates.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Cash and Cash Equivalents&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Cash and cash equivalents include cash maintained in one or more bank accounts. The Company may have bank balances in excess of federally insured amounts&#59; however, the Company deposits its cash and cash equivalents with high credit-quality institutions to minimize credit risk exposure.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Income Tax Information&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company intends to make an election to be taxed as a REIT under Sections 856 through 860 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, commencing with its taxable year ending December&#160;31, 2026. A REIT is subject to several organizational and operational requirements including that it must distribute 90% of its taxable income, subject to certain adjustments, to its shareholders each year. Even if the Company qualifies for taxation as a REIT, it may be subject to certain state and local taxes on its income and property, and federal income and excise taxes on its undistributed income.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Organization and Offering Expenses&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Advisor will advance all the Company&#8217;s organization and offering expenses and certain operating expenses on its behalf through the first anniversary of the initial closing (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Initial Private Wealth Closing</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) of the Company&#8217;s continuous, blind pool private offering (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Private Offering</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) that includes investors other than the Sponsor, the Advisor and&#47;or one or more of their respective affiliates. These expenses may include legal, accounting, printing, mailing, subscription processing and filing fees and other expenses, due diligence expenses of participating broker-dealers supported by detailed and itemized invoices, costs in connection with preparing sales materials, design and website expenses, fees and expenses of the escrow agent and transfer agent, and expense reimbursements for actual costs incurred by employees of the Dealer Manager (as defined below) in the performance of wholesaling activities, but exclude upfront selling commissions, dealer manager fees and the shareholder servicing fees. The Company will reimburse the Advisor for all such advanced expenses ratably over the 60 months following the first anniversary of the Initial Private Wealth Closing.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">After the first anniversary of the Initial Private Wealth Closing, the Company will reimburse all organization and offering expenses incurred by the Advisor as well as certain operating expenses, which as of the date of the filing are estimated to be approximately $640,000. These organization and offering and operating expenses are not recorded on the accompanying consolidated balance sheet because such costs are not the Company&#8217;s liability until the date on which the Company commences operations. When recorded by the Company, organization and operating expenses will be expensed as incurred and offering expenses will be charged to shareholders&#8217; equity. Any amount due to the Advisor but not paid will be recognized as a liability on the consolidated balance sheet.</font></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_483"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 3. Equity</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company is currently authorized to issue an unlimited number of common shares of beneficial interest, par value $0.01 per share. Thereafter, the purchase price per share of each class of common shares will vary and generally will be equal to the prior month&#8217;s NAV per share for such class as of the last calendar day of such month, plus applicable upfront selling commissions and dealer manager fees.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">F-5</font></div></div></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_490"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 4. Related Party Transactions</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Upfront Selling Commissions and Dealer Manager Fees&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Dealer Manager is entitled to receive upfront selling commissions of up to 3.0% of the transaction price of each Class S share sold in the primary offering, however, such amounts may vary at certain participating broker-dealers provided that the sum will not exceed 3.0% of the transaction price of each Class S share sold.  The Dealer Manager may be entitled to receive upfront selling commissions of up to 1.5% of the transaction price of each Class D share sold in the primary offering. The Dealer Manager anticipates that all or a portion of the upfront selling commissions and dealer manager fees will be retained by, or reallowed (paid) to, participating broker-dealers.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">No upfront selling commissions or dealer manager fees are paid with respect to purchases of Class I shares, Class E shares, or shares of any class sold pursuant to the Company&#8217;s distribution reinvestment plan.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Shareholder Servicing Fees&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">LaSalle Investment Management Distributors, LLC, a broker-dealer affiliated with the Advisor, will act as the dealer manager for the Private Offering (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Dealer Manager</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;) pursuant to a dealer manager agreement between the Company and the Dealer Manager. In addition, the Dealer Manager will engage third party broker-dealers and registered investment advisers to participate in the distribution of the offering of common shares.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company will pay the Dealer Manager shareholder servicing fees over time for ongoing services rendered to shareholders by participating broker-dealers or broker-dealers servicing investors&#8217; accounts equal to&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">with respect to outstanding Class S shares, 0.85% per annum of the aggregate NAV of outstanding Class S shares&#59; however, with respect to Class S shares sold through certain participating broker-dealers, the investment professional shareholder servicing fee and the dealer shareholder servicing fee may be other amounts, provided that the sum of such fees will always equal 0.85% per annum of the NAV of such shares&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">with respect to outstanding Class D shares, 0.25% per annum of the aggregate NAV of outstanding Class D shares.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company will not pay a shareholder servicing fee with respect to outstanding Class I shares or Class E shares.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Management Fee&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The services to be provided by the Advisor and the compensation to be paid by the Company will be set forth in the advisory agreement between the Company and the Advisor (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Advisory</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Agreement</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;). Pursuant to the terms of the Advisory Agreement, the Company will pay the Advisor a management fee equal to 1.25% of NAV for its Class S shares, Class D shares and Class I shares, per annum payable monthly.  In addition, to the extent that the Operating Partnership issues units to parties other than the Company, the Operating Partnership will pay LaSalle a management fee equal to 1.25% of the NAV of the Operating Partnership attributable to such Class S, Class D and Class I Operating Partnership units. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The management fee may be paid, at the Advisor&#8217;s election, in cash or Class E shares of the Company, or any combination thereof. The Company will not pay the Advisor a management fee with respect to the Class E shares.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">F-6</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance Fee&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For Class S shares, Class D shares and Class I shares (collectively, the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance Shares</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), the Advisor may be entitled to a performance fee, which is accrued monthly and payable quarterly in arrears. The performance fee generally will be an amount, not less than zero, equal to (i) 12.5% of the Company&#8217;s cumulative Core Earnings (as defined below) for the immediately preceding four calendar quarters (or such shorter period until the Company has operated for four full calendar quarters) (each such period, a &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), subject to a hurdle rate, expressed as an annual rate of return on average adjusted capital, equal to 1.25% per calendar quarter, or 5.0% on an annualized basis (the &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Hurdle Rate</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221;), minus (ii) the sum of any performance fees paid to the Advisor with respect to the first three calendar quarters in the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period. As a result, the Advisor generally does not earn the performance fee for any calendar quarter until the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period exceed the Hurdle Rate.  For purposes of the Performance Fee, &#8220;adjusted capital&#8221; means cumulative net proceeds generated from sales of the Company&#8217;s Performance Shares (including proceeds from the Company&#8217;s distribution reinvestment plan) reduced by distributions from non-liquidating dispositions of the Company&#8217;s investments paid to shareholders holding Performance Shares and amounts paid to shareholders holding Performance Shares for share redemptions pursuant to the Company&#8217;s share redemption program. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">With respect to Class S shares, Class D shares and Class I shares, once the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings exceed the Hurdle Rate, the Advisor is entitled to a &#8220;catch-up&#8221; fee equal to the amount of Core Earnings in excess of the Hurdle Rate, until the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period exceed a percentage of average adjusted capital equal to the Hurdle Rate divided by 0.875 (or 1 minus 0.125) for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period. Thereafter, the Advisor is entitled to receive 12.5% of the Company&#8217;s Core Earnings.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Proportional performance fee calculation methods apply in the periods prior to the period in which the Company has completed four full calendar quarters.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For purposes of calculating the performance fee, &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Core Earnings</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8221; means, for the applicable 4-Quarter Performance Measurement Period, the net income (loss) attributable to shareholders of Performance Shares, computed in accordance with GAAP, including realized gains (losses) not otherwise included in GAAP net income (loss) and excluding (i) non-cash equity compensation expense, (ii) the Performance Fee, (iii) depreciation and amortization, (iv) any unrealized gains or losses or other non-cash items that are included in net income for the applicable reporting period, regardless of whether such items are included in other comprehensive income or loss, or in net income, (v) one-time events pursuant to changes in GAAP, and (vi) certain non-cash adjustments and certain material non-cash income or expense items, in each case after discussions between the Advisor and the Company&#8217;s Independent Trustees and approved by a majority of the Company&#8217;s Independent Trustees.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The performance fee may be paid, at the Advisor&#8217;s election, in cash or Class E shares, or any combination thereof. If the Advisor elects to receive any portion of its performance fee in Class E shares, we may redeem such Class E shares from the Advisor at a later date, at a price per Class E share equal to the NAV per Class E share, as applicable, as of the date of redemption. Class E shares obtained by the Advisor will not be subject to the redemption limits of the share redemption program or any early redemption deduction. The Company will not pay the Advisor a performance fee on Class E shares.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Acquisition Expense Reimbursement</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We will reimburse LaSalle for out-of-pocket expenses in connection with the selection, evaluation, structuring, acquisition, origination and financing of investments, whether or not such investments are acquired or originated. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Operating Expense Reimbursement&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company will reimburse the Advisor and its affiliates for out-of-pocket costs and expenses they incurs in connection with the services they provide to us, including, but not limited to, (1) the actual cost of goods and services used by us, whether payable to an affiliate or a non-affiliated person, including fees paid to administrators, consultants, attorneys, technology providers and other service providers, and brokerage fees paid in connection with the purchase and sale of investments and securities, (2) expenses of managing and operating our investments, whether payable to an affiliate or a non-affiliated person, and (3) expenses related to personnel of the Advisor or its affiliates performing services for us other than those who provide investment advisory services or serve as our executive officers.</font></div><div style="height:72pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">F-7</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company may not reimburse the Advisor at the end of any fiscal quarter for total operating expenses that, in the four consecutive fiscal quarters then ended, exceed the greater of (i) 2% of average invested assets, or (ii) 25% of net income for such four fiscal quarters (determined without reduction for any non-cash reserves and excluding any gain from the sale of assets)&#59; provided, that, to the extent that our total operating expenses exceed these limits and the Independent Trustees determine that the excess expenses were justified based on such factors as they deem sufficient, the Company may be required to reimburse LaSalle for such operating expenses.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loan Fees&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Subject to market conditions allowing, we will seek to have each borrower pay us (or an affiliate thereof) an origination or commitment fee calculated as a percentage of the whole loan on a fully funded basis as determined by the Advisor at the time of the closing of the loan origination. We will pay the Advisor (or affiliate thereof) 50% of any commitment, origination, extension, prepayment, modification or exit fees received for such loans, and 50% will be retained for the benefit of the Company and its shareholders.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Fees from Other Services&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As discussed above, we may retain certain of the Advisor&#8217;s affiliates, including the Sponsor, from time to time, for services relating to our investments or our operations, which may include capital markets services, restructuring services, valuation services, underwriting and diligence services, and special servicing, as well as services related to mortgage servicing, group purchasing, healthcare, consulting&#47;brokerage, loan servicing and asset management, property, title and other types of insurance, management consulting and other similar operational and investment matters. Any fees paid to the Advisor or its affiliates for any such services will not reduce the management fee or performance fee, but will be subject to the approval of a majority of the Independent Trustees as set forth in our Declaration of Trust.  As of September&#160;16, 2026, we have retained an affiliate of the Sponsor for other services to the borrowers in the fixed amount of $5,000 per loan. As of September 15, 2026, the Sponsor has not earned any fees related to these services as no loans have been executed by the Company.</font></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_499"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 5. Economic Dependency</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company is dependent on the Advisor and its affiliates for certain services that are essential to it, including the sale of the Company&#8217;s common shares, acquisition and disposition decisions, and certain other responsibilities. In the event that the Advisor and&#47;or its affiliates are unable or unwilling to provide such services, the Company would be required to find an alternative advisor and alternative service providers.</font></div><div id="i8c2d62ec7a8e48ddbb3d1b160dc31bb4_507"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Note 6.
